questions.q: How does an early voting plan get approved for each county?
questions.a:
Each county board of elections holds a public meeting prior to each election to discuss its county early voting plan. The county board members have the legal authority to create and adopt a plan for the county, and the county elections director will often serve as a resource for the county board in the development of its early voting plan. The State Board does not provide direct input to counties on what sites, days, or times should be in their early voting plans during the county planning stage, but State Board staff may provide general guidance on legal requirements or historical data to assist the county boards.

If the appointed members of a county board unanimously approve a plan, then it goes to the State Board for a final review to ensure it complies with all laws governing early voting plans. If a county board does not unanimously approve a plan, then a member or members of that county board of elections may petition the State Board to adopt a plan for the county. The State Board will then adopt a plan for that county at a public meeting, typically at the State Board office, and when doing so may choose from plans presented or come up with its own plan for the county.

questions.q: What are the requirements for early voting plans under state law?
questions.a:
Proposed plans must meet the dates, times, and locations requirements in N.C.G.S. §§ 163-166.35 and -166.40. The minimum that a county board may choose to offer is early voting only at the board office (or at a nearby “in lieu of” site) during regular business hours on weekdays and from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. on the final Saturday of the early voting period.

The county board may choose to have more opportunities for early voting by opening additional sites or being open for longer hours or on additional weekend days during the early voting period. If it does, then generally those sites must all be open at the same times throughout the early voting period. During the week, that means being open from 8 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. On weekends, that means being open for the same hours. A plan as a whole should not disproportionately favor any party, racial or ethnic group, or candidate.

The State Board may also consider other factors that relate to a specific county, and there are certain requirements for using a building other than the county board office or using private facilities as voting sites. Also, federal law requires voting sites to be accessible for voters with disabilities.

questions.q: What public notice should be given when a county board considers an early voting plan?
questions.a:
Under the N.C. Open Meetings Law (https://www.ncleg.net/enactedlegislation/statutes/html/byarticle/chapter_143/article_33c.html), all official meetings of public bodies must be open to the public, except for closed sessions, which may be held for purposes detailed in the law. County boards should publicly notice their meetings and provide an agenda that is sufficiently worded to allow the public to understand what will be considered at the meeting.

Meeting notices should be sent to the board’s “Sunshine List” (members of the media and public who have requested to receive notices), and posted on the board’s website and on the county board’s principal bulletin board or door of the meeting room. The goal is to ensure that individuals who wish to attend board meetings are made aware of upcoming meetings and agenda items to be considered.

questions.q: Does the county board have to provide copies of any proposed early voting plans before the meeting?
questions.a:
County board meetings will vary in format depending on the county, but the meeting where a county board of elections will be developing its early voting plan is best viewed as a working meeting, where the potential sites, dates, and times that will make up the early voting plans under consideration are discussed and voted on by all board members. Before an early voting planning meeting, there may not be a formulized plan to provide to the public in advance, because the meeting’s purpose is to develop an early voting plan. A county should still make every effort to make available to the public before the meeting any copies of materials that will be presented to the county board members during the meeting, such as a list of potential early voting sites or historical early voting plans for the county. These materials could be posted on the county board’s website or copies made available at the meeting.

 The county board should describe any proposed plan(s) in detail as they are being discussed so attendees can understand what board members are debating and voting on. Written plans and materials – whether proposed or final – are public records and should be provided as promptly as possible upon request.

questions.q: Do county boards of elections have to take public comments about early voting plans – either before the meeting to consider them or at that meeting itself?
questions.a: No. There is no law requiring county boards of elections to receive public comments about early voting plans or any other topic under consideration by the board. As a courtesy, county boards may allow public comments at a meeting or permit interested individuals to submit written comments in advance for consideration by the board. If a county board decides to allow public comments, it should try to ensure everyone has an opportunity to comment but may put time limits on individual speakers or the comment period as a whole.

questions.q: Do county boards have to live stream or record their meetings?
questions.a:
No. Under the Open Meetings Law, public bodies must keep full and accurate minutes of all official meetings. The minutes may be in written form or sound or video recordings. Many county boards allow remote access to and/or record their meetings, but it is not required under state law.

Even though a county board does not have to livestream its meeting, any radio or television station is entitled under state law to broadcast all or any part of the meeting, and any person may photograph, film, record, or otherwise reproduce any part of the meeting, so long as it does not interfere with the meeting.

questions.q: Unsure if You Are Registered?
questions.a: Find out if you are registered to vote by entering your information into the Voter Search (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/).

questions.q: WHO IS ELIGIBLE TO VOTE ABSENTEE?
questions.a: In North Carolina, all registered voters are permitted to vote absentee.

questions.q: HOW DO I REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a:
Registered North Carolina voters must request an absentee ballot with an official NC Absentee Ballot Request Form. There are two ways to access and submit the form:

- Online: NC Absentee Ballot Portal (https://votebymail.ncsbe.gov/app/home).
- On paper: NC Absentee Ballot Request Form, available on the State Board of E (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/vote-mail)le (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/vote-mail)ction (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/vote-mail)s resource page (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/vote-mail).
- After completing the paper form, submit it to your county board of elections, (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) in person or by mail. You may not submit it by fax or email.

questions.q: WHO CAN REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT FOR A VOTER?
questions.a:
- The voter.
- A voter's near relative (spouse, brother, sister, parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, mother-in-law, father-in-law, daughter-in-law, son-in-law, stepparent, or stepchild) or legal guardian on behalf of the voter
- If you need assistance requesting your ballot due to disability, these restrictions do not apply, and you may ask any person to request your ballot.

Anyone requesting a ballot on behalf of a voter will provide their name, address, and relationship to the voter on the absentee request form.

questions.q: WHAT IS THE DEADLINE TO REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: The deadline to request an absentee ballot is two weeks before Election Day by 5pm.

questions.q: DO I HAVE TO REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT FOR EACH ELECTION?
questions.a: Yes. However, if you have a continuous or expected illness or disability, you may request an absentee ballot be sent to you for all elections that you are eligible for in that calendar year. The absentee ballots will be mailed separately at the appropriate time.

questions.q: WHAT IS THE DEADLINE FOR SUBMITTING AN ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: Voted ballots must be received by 7:30pm on Election Day to be counted.

questions.q: WHEN ARE ABSENTEE BALLOTS MAILED OUT TO VOTERS WHO HAVE REQUESTED THEM?
questions.a: Election officials will start mailing out ballots about 60 days before the election to those who have requested them.

questions.q: HOW DO I COMPLETE MY ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a:
One notary public or two witnesses must be in your presence when you mark your absentee ballot. They should only observe you marking your ballot, not how you vote.

Voters who vote by mail must include a photocopy of an acceptable ID. Or they may complete a Photo ID Exception Form with the absentee ballot return envelope. Instructions will be included in the absentee ballot packet. For more information, including acceptable types of photo ID, see Voter ID (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/voter-id).

questions.q: HOW DO I RETURN MY ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a:
Absentee ballots may be returned:

- By mail.
- By commercial courier service. (DHL, FedEx, or UPS.)
- In person at your county board of elections office.
- In person at an open early voting site in your county. You can find early voting sites in your county by using the Early Voting Site Search (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/EVSite/). You may not return an absentee ballot to a polling place on Election Day.

questions.q: CAN I TRACK MY MAILED ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: You can sign up to track your absentee ballot (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/) on your State Board of Elections website.

questions.q: WHAT IF I REQUESTED AN ABSENTEE BALLOT BUT WANT TO VOTE IN PERSON?
questions.a: Requesting an absentee ballot will not record you in the system as having voted. If you do not vote your absentee ballot, you may vote in person during the early voting period or on Election Day. You may simply discard your absentee ballot. There is no need to bring it with you to a polling place.

questions.q: HOW DO I REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT AS AN OVERSEAS OR US MILITARY VOTER?
questions.a:
Overseas citizens and U.S. military personnel can find information on how to register to vote and request an absentee ballot at the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/vote/home.htm)

  Request your Ballot  (https://votebymail.ncsbe.gov/app/home)

questions.q: Does North Carolina allow ballot curing?
questions.a: Yes, North Carolina allows voters to fix an issue with their ballot.

questions.q: How will I know if there’s an issue with my absentee or mail-in ballot?
questions.a: Your county board of elections will contact you if there are any deficiencies with your absentee ballot using the phone number or email address on the absentee request form submitted.

questions.q: What is the deadline to cure my ballot?
questions.a: The deadline to cure (correct) your absentee/mail ballot is noon on the third business day after the election.

questions.q: Can I track my absentee ballot?
questions.a: You can track your ballot by signing up online for status notifications through your state’s online tool. (https://northcarolina.ballottrax.net/voter/)

questions.q: How do I cure a provisional ballot?
questions.a:
The deadline for a provisional voter to show an acceptable photo ID or HAVA ID to their county board of elections is noon on the third business day after the election.

To check the status of a provisional vote, you can use your state’s online tool. (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegProvPIN/)

questions.q: What is a ballot drop box?
questions.a: A drop box is a secure, locked structure operated by election officials where voters can deliver their absentee ballot any time, day or night.

questions.q: Are drop boxes available in my state?
questions.a: No drop boxes are available in North Carolina.

questions.q: Where can I return my ballot?
questions.a:
You can return your voted ballot to your county board of elections office or an open Early Voting site during the Early Voting period.

You can find the location of your county board of elections office here. (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/BOEInfo/)  (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

questions.q: Can I track the ballot after placing in the drop box?
questions.a: No, you can not currently track the status of your voted absentee ballot.

questions.q: Can I vote before Election Day in North Carolina?
questions.a: Yes. In North Carolina, you can vote before Election Day by voting early in person during the early voting period or by voting by mail using an absentee ballot.

questions.q: Do I have to apply to vote early in North Carolina?
questions.a: If you plan to vote early in person, no application is required. If you would like to vote early by mail, you must request an absentee ballot from your county board of elections. Any registered voter in North Carolina may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason.

questions.q: Where can I vote early in person in North Carolina?
questions.a: During the early voting period, you may vote at any early voting site in your county. You can find early voting locations and schedules through your county board of elections. (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

questions.q: How can I receive an early ballot in the mail?
questions.a: Any registered voter in North Carolina can vote by mail by requesting an absentee ballot from their county board of elections. No excuse is required. Read more about requesting and returning your Absentee Ballot here. (https://www.vote411.org/north-carolina#absentee-ballot-process)

questions.q: Do I need an ID to vote early in North Carolina?
questions.a: Yes. Voters are asked to show a photo ID when voting in North Carolina, whether voting early in person or by mail. If you do not have an acceptable ID, you can still vote by completing an ID Exception Form. Read more about voter ID requirements in North Carolina here. (https://www.vote411.org/north-carolina#voter-id-requirements)

questions.q: WHO CAN REGISTER TO VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA?
questions.a:
You can register to vote in North Carolina if you meet all of the following requirements:

- You are a US citizen
- You will be at least 18 years old by the general election
- 16- and 17-year-olds may preregister to vote
- 17-year-olds can vote in a primary if they will turn 18 by the general election
- You have lived in the county where you’re registering for at least 30 days before the election
- The federal Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA) allows certain voters who are active duty military or their families as well as U.S. citizens abroad special rights that provide an expedited means to register and vote by mail-in ballot. Find more information on Military and Overseas Voting (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/military-and-overseas-voting)
- You are not currently serving a felony sentence, including probation, parole, or post-release supervision

questions.q: WHO CAN VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA?
questions.a:
You can vote in North Carolina if you:

- Are a registered voter
- Will be at least 18 years old by the general election
- 17-year-olds can vote in a primary if they will turn 18 by the general election
- Have established residency in the state and county at least 30 days before the election
- Are not currently serving a felony sentence

questions.q: CAN I VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA IF I HAVE A FELONY CONVICTION?
questions.a: Yes, but only after you complete your full sentence. This includes any probation, parole, or post-release supervision. Once your sentence is fully served, you regain your right to vote and can register again.v Voting rights are not restricted by pretrial detention and misdemeanors in North Carolina.

questions.q: CAN I REGISTER AND VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA IF I DON’T HAVE A TRADITIONAL ADDRESS?
questions.a: If you do not have a traditional address, you can draw a picture in the space provided on the voter registration form of your usual sleeping location. Be descriptive and note any nearby streets or physical buildings. You must provide a mailing address if you do not receive mail at your residential address. The mailing address on your registration form can be a P.O. box, local shelter, advocacy organization, outreach center, or the home of someone who will accept mail for you.

questions.q: AM I REQUIRED TO SHOW ID TO REGISTER TO VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA?
questions.a:
Yes, but only certain types of identification are required depending on how you register:

- If you register online, (https://payments.ncdot.gov/) you must provide your NC driver’s license or DMV-issued ID card number, your full Social Security number, and your date of birth
- If you register using a paper form, you must include either:
- Your NC driver’s license number,
- The last 4 digits of your Social Security number, or
- Check a box stating you don’t have either.

questions.q: WHAT TYPES OF ID CAN I USE TO REGISTER TO VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA?
questions.a:
To complete your voter registration online (https://payments.ncdot.gov/) or by paper form, you can use:

- Your North Carolina driver’s license number,
- OR the last 4 digits of your Social Security number.

If you don’t have either and check the corresponding box, you’ll need to show proof of name and address when voting for the first time (examples include a utility bill, government check, bank statement, or paycheck issued within the last 6 months).

If you use Same-Day Registration during Early Voting, you’ll need to show one of the following:

- NC driver’s license or other government-issued photo ID with your current name and address
- Current utility bill, bank statement, government document, paycheck, or government check
- A student document from a NC college/university showing your name and campus address
- A document from the institution that issued the photo ID you're using to vote

questions.q: WHAT IF I DON’T HAVE THE REQUIRED ID WHEN I REGISTER IN NORTH CAROLINA?
questions.a:
You can get a free North Carolina voter photo ID (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/voter-id/get-free-voter-photo-id) in two ways:

- From your county board of elections (no documents required—just your name, DOB, and last four of SSN), or
- From the NC DMV, which offers no-fee state ID cards.

Voters can call or text 844-338-8743 at any time to reach VoteRiders Voter ID Helpline

questions.q: When are official election results available in North Carolina?
questions.a: Official results are never available on Election Day. Election officials are working around the clock to count a large number of ballots, and it’s essential that they take the time to make sure every vote is counted.

questions.q: Where can I find official election results?
questions.a: Official election results will be uploaded on North Carolina’s State Board of Elections website (https://www.ncsbe.gov/results-data/election-results) as they become available.

questions.q: How can I learn more?
questions.a:
What Happens After You Vote in North Carolina (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cRdOKg4kepI) addresses the vote counting process, how voted ballots are stored until Election Day, and other election security measures taken by the NC State Board of Elections.

  Official Results  (https://www.ncsbe.gov/results-data/election-results)

questions.q: What does a poll worker do in North Carolina?
questions.a: Poll workers, called election officials in North Carolina, help run elections by checking in voters, issuing ballots, assisting voters, operating voting equipment, and helping open and close polling places.

questions.q: What qualifications do I need to be a poll worker in North Carolina?
questions.a:
To serve as an election official in North Carolina, you must:

- Be a registered voter in the precinct where you wish to serve
- Complete required training
- Not be a candidate in the election
- Not be a close relative of a candidate in the election
- Not be an elected government official
- Not hold office with a political party
- Not serve as a manager or treasurer for a candidate or political party

North Carolina also allows high school students who are at least 17 years old and in good academic standing to serve as election workers on Election Day through the Student Election Assistant program. Students cannot serve during early voting.

questions.q: Are poll workers paid in North Carolina?
questions.a: Yes. Election officials are paid for their service, and some counties may also provide compensation for training. Pay varies by county and position. Contact your county board of elections (https://www.ncsbe.gov/democracy-heroes-form) for more information.

questions.q: How do I apply to be a poll worker in North Carolina?
questions.a: Sign up online (https://www.ncsbe.gov/democracy-heroes-form) through your state's election worker application or contact your county board of elections (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) to apply.

questions.q: What is a provisional ballot?
questions.a: Provisional ballots ensure that all voters can cast a ballot even if voter eligibility isn’t certain when they vote. Voters can mark a provisional ballot, and election workers set it aside until eligibility is verified at a later time.

questions.q: Does North Carolina offer provisional voting?
questions.a: Yes, North Carolina offers provisional voting.

questions.q: How do I vote a provisional ballot?
questions.a:
You may vote a provisional ballot if you meet specific conditions.

You may be asked to vote a provisional ballot if:

- Your qualification to vote is questioned
- Your voter eligibility is questioned
- Your eligibility to vote a specific ballot is questioned
- You ask to vote for an election that is not in your assigned voting district
- You do not show appropriate ID under HAVA

If you are asked to vote a provisional ballot, that ballot will be held aside until you can prove your eligibility to vote.

questions.q: What are some reasons to vote a provisional ballot?
questions.a:
Examples of reasons for provisional voting:

- There's no record of your registration
- You moved to a different precinct and didn't report the change before 30 days before the election
- You were previously registered in the county but the registration was canceled
- Your address can't be verified in the lookup files
- You're trying to vote at the incorrect precinct
- During a primary election, you try to vote the other parties ballot
- The records indicate you already voted in this election
- Voting during extended hours on Election Day
- Once you vote your provisional ballot you will receive a PIN number in order to check the status of your ballot (http://www.ncsbe.gov/Voting-Options/Provisional-Voting). You can begin checking the status of your ballot 10 days after the election.

questions.q: How do I cure a provisional ballot?
questions.a: The deadline for a provisional voter to show an acceptable photo ID or HAVA ID to their county board of elections is noon on the third business day after the election.

questions.q: How do I check the status of my provisional ballot?
questions.a: Once you vote your provisional ballot you will receive a PIN number in order to check the status of your ballot (http://www.ncsbe.gov/Voting-Options/Provisional-Voting). You can begin checking the status of your ballot 10 days after the election.

questions.q: What voting assistance is available for voters with disabilities?
questions.a:
The Help America Vote Act requires that election authorities have voting equipment for voters with disabilities to vote privately and independently, and North Carolina is no exception.

Voting assistance and curbside voting are offered to voters with disabilities.

CURBSIDE VOTING

Aged and disabled persons allowed to vote outside voting enclosure. In any primary or election any qualified voter who is able to travel to the voting place, but because of age, or physical disability and physical barriers encountered at the voting place is unable to enter the voting place or enclosure to vote in person without physical assistance, shall be allowed to vote either in the vehicle conveying such person to the voting place or in the immediate proximity of the voting place.

VOTING ASSISTANCE

Assistance to voters in primaries and general elections. In a primary or general election, a registered voter qualified to vote in the primary or general election shall be entitled to assistance in getting to and from the voting booth and in preparing his ballots in accordance with the following rules:

1. Any voter shall be entitled to assistance from a near relative of his [her] choice.

2. Any voter in any of the following four categories shall be entitled to assistance from a person of the voter's choice, other than the voter's employer or agent of that employer or officer or agent of the voter's union:

-One who, on account of physical disability, is unable to enter the voting booth without assistance;

-One who, on account of physical disability, is unable to mark his ballots without assistance;

-One who, on account of illiteracy, is unable to mark his ballots without assistance;

-One who, on account of blindness, is unable to enter the voting booth or mark his ballots without assistance.

Please visit your state's resource (http://www.ncsbe.gov/voting-accessibility) for additional information.

For more information on the provisions available for disabled voters, please contact your local election authority (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

questions.q: How do I request accommodation or report accessibility issues?
questions.a: If you have any questions about receiving help in voting, please ask the clerk or inspector at the polling place.

questions.q: Can I vote by mail because of my disability?
questions.a:
Vote-by-mail (absentee voting) is available in North Carolina and no excuse is required. You can find more about how to vote by mail here. (https://www.vote411.org/north-carolina#absentee-ballot-process)

For more information, you can utilize the American Association of People With Disabilities (AAPD) (http://www.aapd.com/what-we-do/voting/) resource.

questions.q: What do I need to register to vote in North Carolina?
questions.a:
Here is what you need to know to register in North Carolina:

There are three methods of voter registration in North Carolina: register in-person, register online (https://www.ncdot.gov/dmv/offices-services/online/Pages/voter-registration-application.aspx%22%20/t%20%22_blank), or email a printable application (https://www.ncsbe.gov/registering/how-register/complete-your-registration-mail%22%20/t%20%22_blank) to your local elections office.

questions.q: Can I register to vote using my college address in North Carolina?
questions.a: Yes, if you consider your campus address your residence, you can register to vote there. If you move to a different dorm or off campus, be sure to update your voter registration with your new address so you vote in the correct district.

questions.q: What’s the deadline to register to vote in North Carolina?
questions.a: North Carolina requires voters to register at least 25 days before the election. Be sure to check the exact date each year. If you miss the deadline, you may still register and vote during early voting, but you cannot change your party affiliation after the deadline.

questions.q: What form of ID do I need to vote in North Carolina?
questions.a: You must present a photo ID when voting in person in North Carolina. This can include a driver’s license, passport, student ID from a state-supported college, or other accepted forms.

questions.q: I’m originally from another state, can I still vote in my home state while studying in North Carolina?
questions.a: Yes, you can vote in your home state using an absentee ballot, but you'll need to follow your home state's rules and deadlines. You can find the rules for your state on VOTE411 or by contacting your state’s election office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm?_ga=2.80770708.201004602.1748545947-889989650.1701105430).

questions.q: Does registering to vote affect my financial aid, parents’ taxes, and/or tuition in North Carolina?
questions.a: Registering to vote in your college community will not affect your Federal Financial Aid, status as a dependent on your parents’ taxes, or tuition status.

questions.q: Does North Carolina require employers to give time off to vote?
questions.a: No. North Carolina law does not require employers to provide time off to vote. Time off to vote is at the employer's discretion. Talk to your employer and make a plan to vote ahead of Election Day.

questions.q: DO I NEED TO SHOW ID WHEN I VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA?
questions.a:
Yes, voters in North Carolina are asked to show a photo ID when voting, whether in person or by mail. However, all voters will be allowed to vote with or without a photo ID. If you don’t have an acceptable ID, you can still vote by completing an ID Exception Form.

Watch: Click here (https://vimeo.com/853456639) to learn about the voter photo ID requirement in all upcoming elections.

questions.q: WHAT TYPES OF ID CAN I USE TO VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA?
questions.a:
You can use any of the following unexpired photo IDs, or IDs that expired less than one year ago:

- North Carolina driver’s license
- Non-driver state ID from the NCDMV
- Driver’s license or ID from another state (only if you registered in NC within 90 days of the election)
- U.S. Passport or Passport Card
- NC voter photo ID from a county board of elections
- Approved college or university student ID
- Approved state, local government, or charter school employee ID

Additional IDs accepted regardless of expiration date:

- Military or veterans ID with photo
- Tribal enrollment card with photo
- Photo ID issued by a government agency for public assistance (if it includes a photo)

For more information, see Voter ID (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncsbe.gov%2Fvoting%2Fvoter-id&data=05%7C01%7Cigarcia-hernandez%40lwv.org%7C3546a4851c6b47972e7b08db56e69bde%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C1%7C0%7C638199320694319483%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=20MUTkI%2F0aICMCxdUdD7ael0cPIJ5N0%2B2BT9z%2FFuQpg%3D&reserved=0) and FAQ: Voter ID (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncsbe.gov%2Fvoting%2Fvoter-id%2Ffaq-voter-id&data=05%7C01%7Cigarcia-hernandez%40lwv.org%7C3546a4851c6b47972e7b08db56e69bde%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C1%7C0%7C638199320694319483%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=d2SR75plmrVdfn4ZdZ4qK1rhX%2BY0uip2zY2hOXBlAgw%3D&reserved=0).

questions.q: WHAT IF I DON’T HAVE AN ACCEPTABLE ID WHEN I GO TO VOTE IN NORTH CAROLINA?
questions.a:
You can still vote. You have two options:

1. Fill out an ID Exception Form at your voting site and vote with a provisional ballot.
2. Vote with a provisional ballot and return to your county elections office by noon on the third business day after the election with your photo ID.

Note: Military and overseas voters casting ballots under special provisions for these voters are required to submit a photocopy of their ID or an ID Exception Form when returning their ballot, even if they are using the overseas online portal.

If voting by mail and you don’t have an acceptable photo ID to include with your ballot, you can complete and include an ID Exception Form instead. All provisional ballots with a truthfully completed ID Exception Form must be counted. Learn more here. (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/voter-id#heading-2)

Voters can call or text 844-338-8743 at any time to reach VoteRiders Voter ID Helpline

questions.q: What is the deadline to register to vote in North Carolina?
questions.a:
- Online registration deadline: 25 days before Election Day
- Register by mail deadline: Postmarked 25 days before Election Day
- In-person registration deadline: 25 days before Election Day. If you missed the voter registration deadline, you may still register (except for party affiliation changes) and vote during early voting.

questions.q: How can I register to vote in North Carolina?
questions.a:
- Register online (https://www.vote411.org/register)
- By mail (English form (https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/Voter_Registration/NCVoterRegForm_06W.pdf) / Spanish Form (https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/Voter_Registration/NCVoterRegForm_09W.pdf))
- Register in person at the DMV (Department of Motor Vehicles)
- Register in person (https://www.ncsbe.gov/registering/how-register/register-person-during-early-voting) during early voting.

questions.q: How can I check my voter registration status?
questions.a: You can verify your voter registration status using North Carolina’s voter information tool. (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/)

questions.q: Does North Carolina have online voter registration?
questions.a: Yes! Use our online registration tool (https://www.vote411.org/register) to complete your application

questions.q: Is same-day voter registration available in North Carolina?
questions.a: No, North Carolina does not have same-day voter registration, but you can register in person during early voting.

questions.q: Can I pre-register to vote?
questions.a: Yes, you can pre-register to vote if you are 16 or 17 years old.

questions.q: Who is eligible to register in North Carolina?
questions.a: Check if you’re eligible to register here (https://www.vote411.org/north-carolina#eligibility-requirements).

questions.q: What types of voting machines does North Carolina use?
questions.a: The voting systems used in North Carolina are Optical Scan, Paper Ballots, and Direct Recording Electronic (DRE).

questions.q: What is optical scan voting?
questions.a:
With optical scan voting, you will receive a card or sheet of paper, which you take over to a private table or booth. The card has the names of the various candidates and ballot measures printed on it.

- With a pen or pencil, you fill in a little box, circle, or space between two arrows.
- When you are finished filling out all the cards, you may bring the cards over to a ballot box, where poll workers will show you how to put the cards in the box.
- Or in some places, you may feed the completed cards or papers into a computer device that checks your card or paper right there at the polling place to make sure you have voted the way you want to and counts the votes.

questions.q: What are paper ballots?
questions.a:
Paper ballots are one of the oldest ways of voting in America.

When you come to the polling place, you will get a paper ballot from the poll worker. You take it to the voting booth, and use a pen or pencil to mark a box next to your candidate and issue choices. You then drop the marked ballot into a sealed ballot box.

questions.q: What is Direct Recording Electronic Voting?
questions.a:
Direct Recording Electronic (DRE) is the newest system in use in the U.S. All the information about who and what you are voting for is on an electronic screen like a TV or computer screen.

There are many variations of DREs because many companies are inventing new ones, and many cities, counties, and states are trying them out.

- Usually, after you have signed in, the poll workers will give you a card that you slide into a device to start your voting session.
- Some of these devices will show all candidates and ballot choices on one big screen. Often, with these big screen devices you push a button next to the name of the candidate you want to vote for (or yes or no on a ballot measure).
- On other DREs, the screen is set up to show pages. There will probably be one thing on which to vote on each screen or page. For example, on one screen or page, you might vote for the president. Then you might move to the next page to vote for a senator. Often these small-screen devices have a touch screen, where you touch the screen next to the name of the person you want to vote for.
- Other devices have a keypad, and some have a keyboard, so you can write in the name of someone you want to vote for.
- You let the system know you are finished voting by pushing a button, touching the screen or entering something on a keypad.

You can learn more about voting systems by checking out the Elections Assistance Commission's (EAC) resource.  (https://www.eac.gov/voting-equipment/system-certification-process)

questions.q: Campaign Finance Information
questions.a:
For information on federal campaign contributions, please visit Open Secrets (http://www.opensecrets.org).

For information on state campaign contributions, please visit your state's resource. (https://www.ncsbe.gov/Campaign-Finance)

questions.q: Candidate and Ballot Measure Information
questions.a: Information on local, state and federal candidates and ballot measures may be available here. (https://www.vote411.org/vote411.org/ballot)

questions.q: Election Dates
questions.a:
The next election date can be found here (https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/upcoming-election).

Contact your local Board of Elections (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for more information.

questions.q: Election Day Voting Hours
questions.a: On Election Day, polling places will be open from 6:30 am to 7:30 pm.

questions.q: Overseas and Military Voters
questions.a:
You are a Military or Overseas voter if you are in uniformed services, living overseas OR a spouse or dependent of a uniformed services voter. To get registered and vote, you can utilize Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)

If you have additional questions about elections and voting overseas you can use our state specific elections official directory or contact the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)

Note: Military and overseas voters casting ballots under special provisions for these voters are required to submit a photocopy of their ID or an ID Exception Form when returning their ballot, even if they are using the overseas online portal.

questions.q: Polling Place Locations
questions.a: You can find your polling place by utilizing your state resource. (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/PPLkup/) If you have further questions on your polling place location, please use the County Board of Elections Search. (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/BOEInfo/)

questions.q: Primary Election Process
questions.a:
North Carolina is a “partially closed” primary state. Each party has the ability to choose whether to allow unaffiliated voters or voters not registered with their party to participate in their primary. This year, unaffiliated voters may choose the ballot of any party that has a primary. This decision is made before the election cycle begins.

In a primary election if a candidate does not with 30% of the votes there will be a primary runoff election scheduled for a few weeks after the primary election date. The runoff election will have the top two candidates with the most votes to ensure that one of them receives the majority of the voters.

If you have any questions about your state’s primary election, please contact your local election officials (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/BOEInfo/).

questions.q: Verify Voter Registration
questions.a:
To verify your voter registration status

  click here!  (https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/)
